title: floodflow — getting-started guide
text: complete run Odaw basin, motivated June 2026 Accra floods. uses synthetic--realistic rainfall runs anywhere; swap real record reproduce basin. Interpreting output: present-day 100-year design rainfall lands near magnitude June 2026 storm, +20% scenario shifts storm shorter return period — kind statement package built make.
code: library(floodflow) set.seed(2026)  # 44-year daily rainfall with a seasonal cycle and a warming trend dates  <- seq(as.Date("1981-01-01"), as.Date("2024-12-31"), by = "day") doy    <- as.integer(format(dates, "%j")) yr     <- as.integer(format(dates, "%Y")) season <- 0.5 + 0.5 * (exp(-((doy - 160)^2) / (2 * 35^2)) +                        0.6 * exp(-((doy - 285)^2) / (2 * 30^2))) cc     <- 1 + 0.030 * (yr - 1981) rain <- data.frame(   date = dates,   precip_mm = round(rbinom(length(dates), 1, 0.28 * season) *                     rgamma(length(dates), 0.7, scale = 9 * season * cc), 1) )  fp <- flood_project("Odaw basin, Accra", crs = "EPSG:32630") fp$rainfall <- rain fp <- flood_extremes(fp) fp <- flood_scenario(fp, method = "delta", change_factor = 1.20,                      scenario_label = "SSP2-4.5 2050") fp <- roughness(fp, method = "constant", value = 0.035) fp <- flood_runoff(fp, lat_deg = 5.6, engine = "simple") fp <- flood_route(fp, method = "muskingum-cunge",                   width = 25, slope = 0.002, area_km2 = 400) fp <- flood_hydraulics(fp, length_m = 12000, overland_m = 200) fp <- flood_uncertainty(fp, observed_depth_m = 4.0, n_sim = 3000, seed = 1)  fp                         # summary of everything run fp$extremes$return_levels  # present-day design rainfall fp$scenario$adjusted       # climate-adjusted design rainfall fp$route                   # peak depth and velocity fp$uncertainty$depth_band  # calibrated depth band

text: flood_extremes() fits generalized extreme value distribution annual maximum rainfall, stationary linear trend location, reports likelihood-ratio test changing extremes together design return levels. dependency-free maximum-likelihood engine used default; extRemes used installed requested. flood_scenario() turns design return levels present-day climate-adjusted event three methods: "delta" (change-factor scaling, default), "trend" (projecting fitted location trend forward) "cmip6" (reserved downscaled projections). roughness() assigns Manning’s roughness three methods: "constant", "landcover" (lookup table, defaulting floodflow_lc_roughness, user-overridable) "ndvi" (monotonic empirical function vegetation index). Works vectors , terra installed, rasters. flood_runoff() converts rainfall discharge series. Potential evapotranspiration computed Oudin formula (pet_oudin()) temperature latitude. GR4J via airGR used installed; otherwise mass-conserving conceptual fallback routing lag runs. flood_route() provides five-method routing ladder turns discharge routed hydrograph water depth: "manning-normal", "kinematic", "diffusive", "muskingum-cunge" (default) "dynamic". Depth comes Manning’s equation; hydrograph routing uses numerically stable Muskingum-Cunge family, varying diffusion across ladder. flood_hydraulics() derives time--motion family routed flow: peak velocity, time concentration Kirpich, Kerby, combined Kerby-Kirpich velocity methods (tc_kirpich(), tc_kerby()), channel travel time, event-relative time--peak. flood_uncertainty() applies Generalized Likelihood Uncertainty Estimation (GLUE): samples roughness width priors, weights run agreement observed depth, returns predictive depth band inverse parameter estimates. Equifinality among parameters reported rather hidden. flood_vulnerability() combines hazard, exposure vulnerability normalised risk index (Risk = Hazard x Exposure x Vulnerability), identifying hotspots deep flooding meets dense, susceptible population. flood_surrogate() trains fast emulator (random forest via ranger, log-linear fallback) depth model rapid -exploration. flood_route() gains optional hand argument: supply Height Nearest Drainage surface (DEM) produces spatial inundation-depth raster, depth_raster, flood_map(layer = "depth") draws real inundation map. flood_map() renders chosen layer (depth, risk, velocity, uncertainty) interactive map via tmap leaflet available, always returns tidy value summary pipeline works without mapping engines.
